data.long_meaning: The name Dariusz is derived from the Polish language and means 'radiant, shining one'. In the Bible, the name Darious is borne by several characters, including a Persian king in the Book of Esther. The name Dariusz carries the meaning “Radiant, shining one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dariusz usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dariusz has its roots in Polish culture and represents the idea of a shining or radiant individual. This name can instill a sense of royalty, strength, and resilience, as there have been several notable figures named Dariusz in Polish history.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Dariusz can serve as a reminder of the inner light or divine spark within each individual, encouraging one to embrace their unique gifts and shining qualities in service of a greater good.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dariusz may symbolize bravery and wisdom in the Christian tradition. As a Polish name derived from Darius, it reflects the Old Persian king known for his strength and rule over vast territories. This name serves as a reminder to stand firm in faith and seek knowledge and understanding.

biblical_reference.note: Darius is mentioned in the Bible as a king who allowed the Jews to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem

historical_references.reference: Dariusz I the Great, also known as Darius I or Xerxes I, was a king of the Achaemenid Empire, ruling from 522 to 486 BC.
historical_references.context: Following the assassination of Xerxes I, Dariusz I seized the throne after defeating the usurper Inaros in battle. He is celebrated as a just and capable ruler who restored Persian authority over the Empire following a period of instability and rebellion.

historical_references.reference: Dariusz II of Persia, also known as Darius Codomannus, was a king of the Achaemenid Empire, ruling from 423 to 404 BC.
historical_references.context: Dariusz II ascended to the throne following the assassination of his father, Xerxes II. He faced numerous rebellions and invasions, including one led by the Spartan king, Archidamus II. Dariusz II is known for his military campaigns to reassert Persian authority, including the defeat of the Greeks at the Battle of Cunaxa.
